title: Standing General Order crash reporting
summary: NHTSA's June 29, 2021 order required named automated-driving and Level 2 driver-assistance developers and operators to report public-road crashes when the system was engaged within 30 seconds. Crashes with a hospital trip, fatality, tow-away, air bag deployment or vulnerable road user were due within one day with a 10-day update; other ADS crashes were monthly. Reports do not establish fault.

title: Third amended Standing General Order
summary: Effective June 16, 2025, NHTSA's third amended crash-reporting order requires covered operators and manufacturers to report serious automated-driving or Level 2 driver-assistance crashes within five days and qualifying less-serious crashes monthly. It differentiates reporting thresholds by automation type, reduces duplicate filings, and requires updates when new information becomes available.

title: AV STEP proposal
summary: NHTSA proposed a voluntary program in which ADS developers, manufacturers and fleet operators would apply for admission, submit independent safety assessments, and accept periodic and event-triggered reporting and public disclosure. It offered two participation levels, including new exemptions for vehicles not meeting all safety standards; comments closed March 17, 2025, and NHTSA withdrew the proposal on June 26, 2026.

title: AV STEP withdrawal
summary: NHTSA withdrew its January 2025 AV STEP proposal on June 26, 2026, after 37 comments argued the voluntary program was complex, unattractive to potential participants and insufficient for oversight. NHTSA added that exemption improvements under its April 2025 AV Framework had already advanced some of the proposal's goals.

title: FMCSA grants Aurora warning-beacon exemption
summary: FMCSA published a notice of final disposition granting Aurora Operations, Inc. a limited five-year exemption for Level 4 automated driving system trucks, allowing cab-mounted warning beacons in place of traditional warning devices. Effective October 7, 2026 through October 7, 2031.

title: NHTSA grants Zoox temporary FMVSS exemption
summary: NHTSA granted Zoox, Inc. a temporary exemption from portions of eight Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards for its automated-driving-system-equipped vehicle, subject to conditions including enhanced oversight. The exemption runs July 31, 2026 through July 31, 2028.

title: NHTSA AV Framework interim exemption guidance
summary: NHTSA published a notice of updates under its AV Framework and requested public comment on interim guidance for commercial deployment exemptions for automated vehicles; the notice set an August 31, 2026 comment deadline (a later notice, 2026-17741, extended it).

title: NHTSA plans updated ADS guidance
summary: NHTSA gave notice of public availability and requested comment on its intent to issue comprehensive updated guidance on safe development and deployment of automated driving systems, releasing draft chapters for comment and later consolidating them into a final document. Comments are due by July 31, 2027.

title: NHTSA fall 2026 research meeting and ADS workshop
summary: NHTSA announced a public meeting on December 1-2, 2026 on its safety research programs. On the afternoon of December 1 the Office of Automation Safety will convene an Automated Driving Systems workshop, which will not be recorded.

title: NHTSA receives Robomart temporary exemption application
summary: NHTSA published a notice that it received Robomart, Inc.'s application for a temporary exemption from several requirements of FMVSS No. 500 for its low-speed vehicle equipped with an automated driving system. NHTSA is conducting an initial review and will later publish a notice seeking public comment on the application's merits.
